verses.commentary: Say to your brothers My People, to your sisters My Loved One. The names reverse. Children told to call siblings by restored names. The chapter begins with future hope before describing present crisis.

Rebuke your mother. The children address the unfaithful wife, Israel. She is not my wife, I am not her husband. Divorce declared. Remove adultery from her face. The makeup and ornaments of prostitution.

I will strip her naked. Public shaming for public unfaithfulness. As bare as on the day she was born. Return to original helplessness. Like a desert, parched land. The promised land becomes wilderness again.
I will not love her children. The children of adultery bear their mother's shame. The family metaphor extends the judgment to all Israel.
She said, I will go after my lovers. Israel's reasoning exposed. The Baals supposedly provided food, water, wool, oil. She credits false gods for covenant blessings. Misattributed gifts.
I will block her path with thornbushes. God obstructs her pursuit of idols. I will wall her in. Gracious frustration. God makes sin difficult to protect from its consequences.
She will chase but not catch. The lovers elude her. Then she will say: I will go back to my husband. When idols fail, the true God becomes attractive again. Desperation as doorway.
She has not acknowledged I gave her the grain. Fundamental ignorance. The silver and gold she used for Baal came from Yahweh. Worshiping idols with covenant gifts.
Therefore I will take away my grain. God reclaims what was misused. Wool and linen withdrawn. The gifts that covered her nakedness removed.
I will expose her lewdness before her lovers. Public humiliation. No one will rescue her from my hand. The lovers are powerless against the husband.
I will stop all her celebrations. Festivals, New Moons, Sabbaths. Religious calendar cancelled. The joy of worship ends when the heart has left.
I will ruin her vines and fig trees. What she thought was payment from lovers, I will destroy. Orchards become thickets. Cultivation returns to wild.
I will punish her for the days she burned incense to Baals. The decorated adulteress who forgot me. Memory of God lost in the pursuit of others.

Therefore I will allure her. The turn. After judgment, seduction. I will lead her into the wilderness. Back to the honeymoon place, where Israel first knew God. Speak tenderly. Literally, speak to her heart.

I will give back her vineyards. Restoration of what judgment removed. The Valley of Achor (trouble) becomes a door of hope. The place of Achan's sin (Joshua 7) becomes entrance to blessing. She will respond as in her youth. Egypt's departure relived.
You will call me my husband (ishi). No longer my master (baali). The Baal terminology purged even from proper address. Intimacy replaces servitude.
I will remove the names of the Baals from her lips. Even the memory erased. The false gods no longer invoked.
A covenant for them with the animals. New Eden. Predators pacified. Bow and sword abolished. Safety throughout the land.
I will betroth you to me forever. Betrothal repeated three times. In righteousness, justice, love, compassion. The wedding gifts are character traits. God gives himself.
I will betroth you in faithfulness. The final term. You will acknowledge the Lord. Knowledge of God restored. The relationship rebuilt.
I will respond to the skies. A chain of response: God to heavens, heavens to earth, earth to grain, wine, oil. The whole creation participates in restoration.
They will respond to Jezreel. The name of scattering becomes the name of planting. God sows his people in the land. Agricultural imagery of restoration.

I will plant her in the land. Permanent settlement. I will say to Not My People, You are my people. The divorce reversed. They will say, You are my God. Covenant restored, both sides speaking the old words again.
